name: copy
reason: Still todo by its note, so the verdict stays until re-review: getMethodAttr now mirrors getattr(self, name) with both AttributeError cases and CopyShallow pins every kind, __copy__ and the reduce tuple, but the mirror still has no copyreg.dispatch_table step (:84-86) and no __reduce_ex__ = None -> __reduce__ fallback (:92-94).

name: deepcopy
reason: Still todo by its note, so the verdict stays until re-review: DeepcopyPaths now pins atoms, str and type-classes before the memo read (:118 before :125) and every later branch, so the str-before-memo gap is closed, but the mirror still lacks copyreg.dispatch_table (:139-141), the __reduce_ex__ = None -> __reduce__ fallback (:143-149) and _keep_alive (:161); also deepAttrs stores a copied non-str __dict__ key without hashing it, where CPython's _deepcopy_dict of the state (:201) raises the unhashable TypeError when memo sends that key to a mutable copy.

name: _deepcopy_list
reason: Unaffected by the key change: y allocated and in memo before the items are copied in order, first failure stops it (:172-177); DeepcopyMemo (self-list cycle), DeepcopyAliasing, DeepcopyListExact and DeepCopyOrder rule out reversed order, late memo and lost sharing.

name: _deepcopy_tuple
reason: Unaffected: copies, second memo read, identity zip (:181-194); DeepcopyTupleIdentity pins y = x, DeepcopyTupleExact the new tuple and the t = ([t],) second read, so always-new or never-reread versions fail.

name: _deepcopy_dict
reason: deepPairs/dictSet are unchanged apart from storeItem becoming generic over the key type (the Nat instance is the same function): memo first, value before key (:201), hash then insertdict's in-place merge (Objects/dictobject.c:2001-2049, :2748-2759); DeepcopyDictExact, DeepcopyDictMerge and DeepCopyOrder fail key-first, append-always and last-key-wins versions.

name: _deepcopy_frozendict
reason: Unaffected: a fresh dict through the same store with no memo entry, then the memo read, then a new frozendict (:206-217); DeepcopyFrozendict pins always-new, memo-wins and first-failure.

name: _deepcopy_method
reason: Unaffected by the attribute-key change (an inst __self__ is copied through deepAttrs, which only the deepcopy row depends on): the exact result is pinned by DeepcopyMethod and the missing second memo read by the refuted DeepcopyMethodAliasing, whose counterexample runs this body, with bugs/corelibs-copy-method-aliasing.yaml.

name: _keep_alive
reason: Still todo and not modelled: memo[id(memo)] = [..., x] is visible to a caller-supplied memo, to __deepcopy__(memo) and to deepcopy(memo, memo), and the heap has no cell for the memo; kept here so prefill does not re-credit it.

name: _reconstruct
reason: The None-state check (:252), y.__dict__ before the state (:263), dict_update_arg's mapping vs pair-sequence split with merge_from_seq2's exact ValueError and TypeError (Objects/dictobject.c:3992-4005, :4052-4112), setattr's str-name check, in-place dict stores for update, setattr and __setstate__ (storeItem on tagged keys), fallible iterators and listiter before dictiter are all mirrored; ReconstructSteps (new and existing name), ReconRestItems, ReconstructDeepSteps, ReconstructMemoFirst, DeepcopyStateNone and DeepcopyIterFails fail versions that call __setstate__ on None, move an updated key, read the state before y.__dict__, ignore an iterator's error or swap the loops; scope: dictiter items are pairs, observationally the same as an iterator that raises at that item.

name: replace
reason: Unchanged since the last pass: obj.__class__ (abstract clsOf), getattr(cls, '__replace__', None) with an explicit None giving the same TypeError naming cls.__name__, then func(obj, **changes) (:296-300); ReplaceCall pins both None cases and the exact call, so dropping changes, ignoring a None attribute or always raising fails; a __class__ or metaclass getattr that raises something other than AttributeError is not expressible.
